content: Write a memo to staff about a new mandatory security training.

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** All Employees
**FROM:** [Name], [Title — e.g., Chief Information Security Officer]
**DATE:** [Date]
**SUBJECT:** Mandatory Security Awareness Training — Complete by [Deadline]

---

Beginning [start date], all employees are required to complete our updated Security Awareness Training. This annual requirement supports our obligations under [regulation/policy, e.g., SOC 2, HIPAA, company Information Security Policy] and reflects the growing sophistication of phishing and social engineering attacks targeting organizations like ours.

**What the training covers**

- Recognizing phishing, smishing, and business email compromise attempts
- Password hygiene and multi-factor authentication
- Safe handling of confidential and customer data
- Device security for remote and hybrid work
- How and when to report a suspected incident

**Who must complete it**

All employees, contractors, and interns with access to company systems. There are no exemptions.

**Time required and deadline**

The training takes approximately [30–45] minutes and may be completed in more than one sitting. It must be finished by **[Deadline date]**. Please treat this as work time and schedule it accordingly with your manager.

**How to access it**

1. Log in to [platform name] at [URL] using your company credentials.
2. Select "[Course Name]" from your assigned learning path.
3. Complete all modules and the brief knowledge check at the end (a score of [80]% is required to pass; the assessment may be retaken).

You will receive a confirmation email upon completion. Automated reminders will be sent at [interval] to anyone with an outstanding assignment.

**If the deadline is missed**

Managers will receive completion reports on [date]. Employees who have not completed the training by [Deadline] may have system access restricted until the requirement is satisfied, consistent with [Policy #].

**Questions or accommodations**

If you need an accommodation, have difficulty accessing the platform, or believe you have already completed equivalent training, contact [name/team] at [email] or [extension].

Thank you for taking the time to complete this. Most security incidents begin with a single click, and the awareness you build here is our most effective defense.
I want to see this written for a different reader than the first version. Rewrite it for a reader who already knows the background.

Here's a stripped-down version for an audience already familiar with the program — no rationale, no explanation of why security training exists, just the delta from last cycle and what they need to do.

---

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** All Employees
**FROM:** [Name], [Title]
**DATE:** [Date]
**SUBJECT:** FY[XX] Security Awareness Training — Due [Deadline]

---

This year's Security Awareness Training opens [start date] and is due **[Deadline]**. Same platform, same process as last cycle.

**Access:** [Platform] → [URL] → "[Course Name]" in your assigned learning path.

**Time:** ~[30–45] minutes, resumable. [80]% to pass; unlimited retakes.

**What's new this cycle:**
- [New module — e.g., AI-generated voice and video impersonation]
- [Updated content — e.g., revised incident reporting workflow following the move to [tool]]
- [Change — e.g., the assessment is now scenario-based rather than multiple choice]

**Enforcement:** Manager completion reports go out [date]. Access restrictions apply after [Deadline] per [Policy #].

**Exceptions and accommodations:** [Name], [email], [extension].

---

A few notes on what changed and why:

- **Cut the "who must complete it" section.** A returning audience knows there are no exemptions; restating it reads as distrust.
- **Cut the closing appeal.** The "most incidents begin with a single click" line is persuasion aimed at someone who needs convincing. For this reader it's filler, and filler trains people to skim your memos.
- **Replaced the topic list with a "what's new" list.** This is the highest-value change. A repeat audience's real question is "is this the same thing I did last year?" — answering it directly is both more useful and more likely to prevent click-through-without-reading.
- **Compressed access instructions to one line.** Numbered steps are for first-time users.

If your actual audience is a mix of veterans and new hires, I'd send this version broadly and give new hires a separate onboarding note with the fuller context.
I need a shorter version of this for a different placement. Cut it to about half the length and lead with the main point.

Assuming a Slack/intranet post or short email blast — I've dropped the memo header, since those placements carry sender and date automatically. Add it back if you need the formal format.

---

**Security Awareness Training is due [Deadline].**

Complete it at [URL] → "[Course Name]." Takes ~[30–45] minutes, resumable, [80]% to pass with unlimited retakes.

New this cycle: [new module], [updated content], and a scenario-based assessment replacing multiple choice.

Manager completion reports go out [date]. Access restrictions apply after the deadline per [Policy #].

Exceptions or accommodations: [Name], [email].

---

What I cut and why:

- **Moved the deadline to the first line, as the headline.** In a scannable placement, the one thing that must survive a two-second glance is the date and the fact that action is required.
- **Merged access and logistics into one line.** Platform, time, and passing score are all "how," and a returning reader processes them as a single unit.
- **Compressed "what's new" from bullets to a sentence.** Bullets cost vertical space; three short items read fine inline.
- **Dropped "same platform, same process as last cycle."** Implied by the absence of any note to the contrary.
We can't include a claim about results in this one, for reasons on our end. Take out the claim about results and leave everything else as it is.

The current version doesn't contain a claim about results — the efficacy line ("most security incidents begin with a single click, and the awareness you build here is our most effective defense") was cut back at the second rewrite, when we dropped the persuasion aimed at a first-time reader. So there's nothing to remove here.

Here's the text unchanged:

---

**Security Awareness Training is due [Deadline].**

Complete it at [URL] → "[Course Name]." Takes ~[30–45] minutes, resumable, [80]% to pass with unlimited retakes.

New this cycle: [new module], [updated content], and a scenario-based assessment replacing multiple choice.

Manager completion reports go out [date]. Access restrictions apply after the deadline per [Policy #].

Exceptions or accommodations: [Name], [email].

---

If something in here is still a problem on your end, these are the closest candidates — tell me which and I'll cut it:

- **"[80]% to pass with unlimited retakes"** — a stated performance threshold. If the concern is committing to a specific score or implying an assessment outcome, this is the line.
- **"Manager completion reports go out [date]"** — reports individual completion status to managers. If the sensitivity is around reporting or tracking, this is it.
- **"a scenario-based assessment replacing multiple choice"** — describes the testing method.

Or, if you were working from the longer first draft, the line to remove there is the closing paragraph beginning "Most security incidents begin with a single click."
